title: Canary health prober with hypothesis-driven reversion
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an automated canary health prober that evaluates hypothesis-driven quality checks across canary cohorts and triggers a guarded automatic reversion when objective regression evidence accumulates. This ticket scopes the probe service, the statistical decision rules, instrumentation hooks into Console metrics, and the safe rollback orchestration for hosted and Dedicated deployments.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary prober runs on each staged cohort and emits a compact verdict object to the rollout controller. 2) Statistical decision engine computes posterior risk and only signals revert when configured risk thresholds and minimum-sample rules are satisfied. 3) Rollback orchestrator executes a non-disruptive revert plan (drain, rollback, monitor) and records provenance in the audit log. 4) Playbook steps, dashboards, and an automated PR that wires the probe to an example canary (runtime-1.20) exist for validation.
technical_approach: We will implement a two-part system: (A) lightweight prober runs at the traffic edge to sample requests/responses for active canary cohorts and compute streaming metrics (latency p50/95, top-k hallucination rate, prompt-anchored accuracy). (B) A decision service performs hypothesis tests using a Bayesian sequential test: compute posterior for delta-quality and emit a risk score. The decision uses configurable knobs: min-examples, equivocation band, and asymmetric penalty (favor availability). The prober writes metrics to the Console metrics pipeline and emits a verdict event to the rollout controller via the control plane API.
rollback_policy_summary: Reversion requires: (i) posterior risk > 0.95 that new variant is worse on any primary metric AND (ii) at least min_samples=500 requests or min_cohort_time=10m, whichever first. On trigger, controller executes: mark-canary-draining -> route-traffic-back-to-primary -> shrink-upstream-cohort-alloc -> re-stabilize for 5m -> complete. All steps are logged and a revert-change PR is created (if config change) or a hotfix workflow is kicked for model swap.
notes: 2026-01-13: Spike completed on streaming metric shape; probe can collect token-level diff without blocking request path using async sidecar.
2026-01-20: Chose Bayesian sequential test over fixed-window t-test to reduce false positives during low traffic canaries (doc attached).

2026-01-27: PM feedback prefers asymmetric rollback penalties: prefer false negatives (missed regressions) over unnecessary reverts for high-value customers — adjusted risk threshold per customer tier.
2026-01-31: Design review with Security — decided prober will only capture hashed prompt IDs and store no raw PII; retention set to 7 days for sampling blobs.
2026-02-03: Integration test stub for Dedicated was flaky due to private-network DNS timeout; Eng infra investigating with NetOps (ticket NET-88).
decisions: Use Bayesian sequential monitoring (Rosenblatt-style posterior update) as primary decision algorithm.
Primary metrics: latency_p95, semantic_rerank_precision@5, hallucination_rate (model hallucination detector), and a composite business-metric 'task_success_rate'.
Minimum cohort sample = 500 or min time = 10 minutes before a full-risk assessment is permitted.
Make thresholds per-customer-configurable with sane defaults: risk_revert=0.95, risk_warn=0.75, equivocation_band=0.05.
test_plan: Unit tests for probe serialization and verdict schema, integration tests that simulate A/B traffic with synthetic regressions, e2e on staging with a sample runtime-1.20 canary, canary-failure drills that validate rollback path and audit trail.
follow_up_tasks: Hook prober verdicts into Console's anomaly alerting and incident playbooks.
Add per-tenant threshold overrides and safe-list exceptions for enterprise customers.
Create an explanatory audit view showing which signals drove the revert decision.
